definition: A multilingual notation is a representational system designed to encode, describe, or annotate information in a way that is usable across multiple natural languages without being tied to any single one.
details: It is especially relevant in fields like computational linguistics, lexicography, and knowledge representation.

explainer.lead: A multilingual notation encodes or annotates information so it works across several natural languages without belonging to any one. It matters where data must stay language-neutral, as in lexicography and knowledge representation.

tiers.eli5: Like a set of symbols on road signs that drivers from any country can read without knowing the local language.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use such notations to store meaning separately from surface wording, so the same record serves many languages. A pitfall is that language-neutral schemes can lose nuances only one language expresses.
tiers.paperLevel: A representational system whose symbols and structure are decoupled from any single natural language, usable for encoding, describing or annotating information across languages. Limits: coverage of language-specific distinctions is inherently partial.

explainer.example: A dictionary entry stores a concept identifier and structured fields once, with per-language labels attached, so the same entry renders in English, French and Arabic.
